elements.text: Thousands of Revolutionary War veterans had not been paid for their military service. Without other sources of money, many veterans were left poor after the war.

He was shocked to discover that he was being called to court for not paying off his debts. Shays did not have the money to pay his debt because he had not yet been paid for his service in the war. To address the problems with the Articles of Confederation, a group of congressmen called for a meeting of all the states. That meeting would later be known as the Constitutional Convention.

pieces.text: But before the states could meet,
broke out in Massachusetts. Read about the Shays's Rebellion crisis. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: In the 1780s, Revolutionary War veteran Daniel Shays returned home to his farm in western Massachusetts. He was shocked to discover that he was being called to court for not paying off his debts. Shays did not have the money to pay his debt because he had not yet been paid for his service in the war. Shays was furious—the state government was punishing him for not paying his debts, but the central government hadn't even paid him for fighting in the war!
Many farmers in western Massachusetts were in the same situation as Shays. When the farmers could not pay their debts, the Massachusetts state courts began seizing the farmers' land and property.

pieces.text: Angered at the courts, Shays and other farmers felt they had no choice but to use force. They marched to the courthouses with pitchforks, clubs, and muskets and refused to let the courts meet. Fearing the mobs, the Massachusetts governor assembled a
to fight the farmers. The battles between the state militia and the farmers ended with 4 dead and 20 wounded.

meaning.text: a group of volunteers who fight in emergencies

It showed that farmers were joining forces with Native Americans.
It showed that the new nation's problems could lead to violence.
It showed that all Americans were united against the central government.

content.text: The size of the U.S. increased in the years after the American Revolution.

want to expand the country.

content.text: In the early 1800s, the U.S. fought wars against Spain and France in North America.

explanationText.text: The timeline says that the U.S. acquired territory from Spain and France. It does not say that the U.S. fought wars against either country.

contents.text: In the early 1800s, Great Britain, France, Spain, and the Netherlands each had colonies in the Caribbean that produced valuable goods like sugar and tobacco. But once these countries became involved in the Napoleonic Wars, they could not easily transport goods from their colonies to Europe. Because the United States was neutral in the European war, the conflict created an opportunity for American merchants.
Sort the following into categories indicating whether they represent an opportunity or a risk for the United States.

label.text: American merchants could make a lot of money by carrying goods from European colonies in the Caribbean to American ports, then re-exporting them to Europe.
American farmers could sell their agricultural products to Britain and France, which needed them as war supplies.
American ships could be seized by the British and French navies, which did not want the supplies to reach their opponents.

contents.text: Read the passage. These choices are correct:

content.text: Captured sailors were treated poorly and blamed when things went wrong.

explanationText.text: In the passage, James M'Lean is forced by the captain to let out a sail. When the sail rips, M'Lean is blamed and punished with a severe lashing.

content.text: British officers claimed that American sailors were actually British.

explanationText.text: The passage says that James M'Lean showed proof of citizenship from New York, but English captain John Dilks did not believe him. Captain Dilks said "It is of no use for you to pretend that you are an American, for you was born in Britain."

contents.text: These choices are not correct:

content.text: British officers treated impressed sailors better than their own countrymen.

explanationText.text: The passage says the opposite. In the passage, M'Lean is punished harshly after he is blamed for damaging a sail.

content.text: American sailors could easily prove that they were citizens of the United States.

explanationText.text: The passage says the opposite. In the passage, M'Lean attempts to prove that he is a U.S. citizen, but the British captain does not accept his proof of citizenship.

elements.text: In 1815, Jackson was in command of American troops defending New Orleans from the British.

contents.text: Jackson was popular in Tennessee, but to become president he had to win support in eastern states, too. So, his friends wrote letters about him to eastern newspapers.

The passage below is from a letter published in a newspaper in Pennsylvania in 1824, during Jackson's first presidential campaign. It tells an especially important story about something Jackson did when he was a teenager.

header.text: Read the passage. Then follow the instructions below.

textContent.text: [During the Revolutionary War,] Jackson, then only about 14 or 15 years of age, [became] a volunteer in the [military] service of his country. He was taken prisoner, when a British officer…commanded him to brush [the officer's] boots. Young as he was, he…refused to do as he was ordered, and demanded to be treated as a prisoner. The officer (and a contemptible fellow he must have been), aimed a blow at him with his sword, by which [Jackson's] hand, thrown up for defense, was [almost cut off].

meaning.text: treated fairly, as required by the laws of war

header.text: Andrew Jackson was a famous general when he decided to run for president in 1824. Jackson's military career was a major topic of discussion during the campaign. People often talked about two parts of Jackson's military record:

elements.text: In 1815, Jackson was in command of American troops defending New Orleans from the British.
In 1818, Jackson and his troops were defending Americans from a group of Native Americans, the Seminoles. They chased the Seminoles into Florida, which at that time was part of Spain's empire.

contents.text: Some Americans used these events to argue that Jackson would be a great president. Others used them as evidence that he would be a dangerous president.

contents.text: Jackson was popular in Tennessee, but to become president he had to win support in eastern states, too. So, his friends wrote letters about him to eastern newspapers.

The passage below is from a letter published in a newspaper in Pennsylvania in 1824, during Jackson's first presidential campaign. It tells an especially important story about something Jackson did when he was a teenager.

header.text: Read the passage. Then follow the instructions below.

textContent.text: [During the Revolutionary War,] Jackson, then only about 14 or 15 years of age, [became] a volunteer in the [military] service of his country. He was taken prisoner, when a British officer…commanded him to brush [the officer's] boots. Young as he was, he…refused to do as he was ordered, and demanded to be treated as a prisoner. The officer (and a contemptible fellow he must have been), aimed a blow at him with his sword, by which [Jackson's] hand, thrown up for defense, was [almost cut off].

content.text: The American population grows rapidly. There are more people who want land to farm.

elements.text: Native American tribes controlled large areas of extremely fertile land, especially in the South. When the population increased, there was less land for each person to farm.

content.text: New technology makes it easier to farm and to sell crops. More people want to have land so they can farm and make money from it.

elements.text: New farming technology made it easier to make money through farming. More people wanted to take Native American land and use it to farm and sell crops.

content.text: In the South, it is legal to own enslaved people and use their labor to grow profitable crops like cotton. Many white slaveowners wanted more land to grow cotton.

elements.text: The "Five Civilized Tribes" controlled land in the South where some of their members owned enslaved people and grew profitable crops such as cotton. After seeing their success, some white Americans wanted to take their land and do the same.

content.text: Gold is discovered on Cherokee land. White Americans want access to the gold.

elements.text: When gold was discovered on Cherokee land, some white Americans wanted it for themselves. People illegally invaded Cherokee land and began looking for and taking gold.

contents.text: Although they had adopted American practices, the "Five Civilized Tribes" in the South still did not want to give up their land. So, white settlers began to take the tribes' land from them, often with the help of state governments.

In the South, it is legal to own enslaved people and use their labor to grow profitable crops like cotton. Many white slaveowners wanted more land to grow cotton.
Gold is discovered on Cherokee land. White Americans want access to the gold.
The American population grows rapidly. There are more people who want land to farm.

pieces.text: All of these events
white Americans' desire to take Native American land:

content.text: New technology makes it easier to farm and to sell crops. More people want to have land so they can farm and make money from it.

elements.text: New farming technology made it easier to make money through farming. More people wanted to take Native American land and use it to farm and sell crops.

content.text: In the South, it is legal to own enslaved people and use their labor to grow profitable crops like cotton. Many white slaveowners wanted more land to grow cotton.

elements.text: The "Five Civilized Tribes" controlled land in the South where some of their members owned enslaved people and grew profitable crops such as cotton. After seeing their success, some white Americans wanted to take their land and do the same.

content.text: Gold is discovered on Cherokee land. White Americans want access to the gold.

elements.text: When gold was discovered on Cherokee land, some white Americans wanted it for themselves. People illegally invaded Cherokee land and began looking for and taking gold.

content.text: The American population grows rapidly. There are more people who want land to farm.

elements.text: Native American tribes controlled large areas of extremely fertile land, especially in the South. When the population increased, there was less land for each person to farm.

contents.text: Although they had adopted American practices, the "Five Civilized Tribes" in the South still did not want to give up their land. So, white settlers began to take the tribes' land from them, often with the help of state governments.

header.text: Leaders of the Cherokee Nation developed new laws to help them defend their land. In 1827, they wrote a new constitution for the Cherokee Nation based on the U.S. Constitution. Look at statements from the Cherokee constitution. Then follow the instructions below.

property of the [Cherokee] Nation.

header.text: Look back at the statements from the Cherokee constitution.

pieces.text: The first statement says that the boundaries, or borders, of the Cherokee Nation will forever remain the same. In other words, the borders would
change.
The second statement says that the land will remain the common property of the Cherokee Nation, or property that is shared by all the people in the Cherokee Nation. In other words, the land
be divided and sold.
